(i) the bulk of the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC shows efficient equilibration and hydrodynamical evolution; and (ii) the hydrodynamically expanding matter is a strongly interacting, deconfined quark-gluonic plasma.

hydrodynamic models provide a good description of most of the measured particle spectra and elliptic flow data at RHIC energies, but fail to reproduce the two-particle correlations.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the hydrodynamic description of heavy ion collisions is a robust and powerful tool for extracting information about the early stages of the collision and the properties of the hot and dense medium created in these collisions.
